$schemaNote: One entry per (repo, secret name) pair — a same-named secret must be configured separately in each repo's own GitHub Secrets store (org-level secrets are the one exception; see the Ralph entries below), and can lapse in one repo while staying healthy in another. Field meanings: purpose (why this secret exists, grounded in the workflow that reads it), breaksWhenMissing (the actual observable failure — not a guess), rotateUrl (where a human gets/regenerates the credential), secretUrl (where it's stored, i.e. the repo's GitHub Actions secrets page), probe (one of github-token-expiry | npm-whoami | figma-me | supabase-select | presence — see scripts/check-secret-health.mjs), probeStrength ('verified' = the probe authenticates against the live service; 'presence-only' = the probe can only confirm the env var is set and non-empty, never that the value still works). Built for ops#415, verified against */.github/workflows/ on 2026-09-22 — see that issue's session report for what was checked and what could not be.

secrets.name: SUPABASE_URL
secrets.purpose: Base URL of the ops Supabase project (vvyccwxtcwvlusweenje), paired with SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY to read/write the leads/tasks board from CI (comb-tasks.yml's manual comb job, site-audit.yml's PageSpeed pass).
secrets.breaksWhenMissing: comb-tasks.yml and site-audit.yml can't construct a Supabase client — both fail at their 'Check required secrets' step before doing any work.

secrets.name: SUPABASE_SERVICE_ROLE_KEY
secrets.purpose: Full-access Supabase service-role key, deliberately confined to the two workflows that need it (comb-tasks.yml's manual comb job, site-audit.yml) rather than the general @claude executor, so a DB key is never handed to an arbitrary issue commenter (ops#49/#54).
secrets.breaksWhenMissing: Same two workflows fail at their secrets-check step; the manual 'Comb tasks board' run and the scheduled PageSpeed site audit both stop reading/writing the leads/tasks tables.

secrets.name: SUPABASE_ACCESS_TOKEN
secrets.purpose: Personal access token for the Supabase Management API — the only way to read supabase_migrations.schema_migrations (PostgREST doesn't expose that schema). Used by check-migration-ledger.mjs (ops#348) and check-production-health.mjs's direct project-status check (ops#318/#347).
secrets.breaksWhenMissing: check-migration-ledger.mjs skips loudly instead of comparing the ledger (by design — it never reports 'in sync' for a ledger it couldn't read); check-production-health.mjs's Management-API status check is skipped, leaving only the /api/tasks row-count check as the live-health signal.

secrets.name: FIGMA_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN
secrets.purpose: Pushes the compiled token set to the Figma Variables REST API whenever hirobius.tokens.json changes on main (sync-figma-variables.yml).
secrets.breaksWhenMissing: The 'Push variables to Figma API' step 401s. hirobius.figma-variables.json still commits (that part doesn't need the token), but the live Figma file stops updating — tokens and design drift apart silently.
secrets.rotateUrl: https://www.figma.com/settings (Security tab → Personal access tokens — the exact path the workflow's own header comment documents)

secrets.name: FIGMA_FILE_KEY
secrets.purpose: The target Figma file's key (from its URL, figma.com/design/{FILE_KEY}/...) — an identifier, not a credential, but stored as a secret because it's only ever consumed alongside FIGMA_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN in the same step.
secrets.breaksWhenMissing: sync-figma-variables.yml can't build the target API URL at all — the push step fails before it can even attempt auth.
secrets.rotateUrl: https://www.figma.com/files/recent (locate the shared Hirobius library file and copy the key from its URL)

secrets.name: OPS_AGENT_KEY
secrets.purpose: Bearer token /ops's protected API routes accept for headless/agent callers (lib/ops-auth.mjs, checkAgentKey), bypassing the password-cookie flow. Set identically in Vercel (so the deployed app accepts it) and here (so CI can call it) — see check-production-health.mjs.
secrets.breaksWhenMissing: check-production-health.mjs (ops#318, runs every 6h) can't authenticate its GET /api/tasks probe — the one automated signal built to catch a silently-broken /ops (ops#347: paused Supabase behind a clean 200 { tasks: [] }) goes dark without anyone knowing.

secrets.name: RALPH_WATCHDOG_TOKEN
secrets.purpose: Fine-grained GitHub PAT the watchdog uses in place of the built-in GITHUB_TOKEN (ralph-watchdog.yml: `secrets.RALPH_WATCHDOG_TOKEN || secrets.GITHUB_TOKEN`) — needed because Actions' own ephemeral token can't trigger downstream workflow runs (the anti-recursion guard; see hds's RELEASE_PAT fix for the same failure mode in a different workflow).
secrets.breaksWhenMissing: Falls back to GITHUB_TOKEN automatically, so the workflow itself doesn't error — but that fallback silently re-introduces the exact recursion-guard deadlock this token exists to avoid. Worth alerting on even though nothing turns red.

secrets.name: PAGESPEED_API_KEY
secrets.purpose: Google PageSpeed Insights API key for the scheduled site-audit.yml Core Web Vitals pass across client sites.
secrets.breaksWhenMissing: site-audit.yml fails at its 'Check required secrets' step before running the audit — client site performance scores stop being collected.

secrets.name: PII_DENYLIST
secrets.purpose: Out-of-repo list of real client/contact identifiers check-pii.mjs matches against, so the denylist content is never itself committed (ops#27/#35). Read pre-commit, on every PR/main push, and weekly across the fleet.
secrets.breaksWhenMissing: check-pii.mjs still runs but matches only its generic patterns (emails/phones measured at ~11% precision in the 2026-09-16 sweep) — the denylist-term and private-workspace-link rules that actually block a commit go dark silently unless something surfaces the gap.
secrets.rotateUrl: https://github.com/hirobius/ops/settings/secrets/actions (edit the value directly — this is curated data, not a vendor-issued credential)

secrets.name: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN
secrets.purpose: Auth for the fleet's dispatched-task executor (claude.yml, comb-tasks.yml, ralph-metric.yml) — runs Claude Code on Adrian's Max subscription rather than a metered API key.
secrets.breaksWhenMissing: Every @claude-mentioned issue/comment stops being picked up; the Ralph metric batch runner and the manual task-comb job both fail at the Claude Code step.
secrets.rotateUrl: run `claude setup-token` locally (per claude.yml's own setup comment), then update the secret

secrets.name: DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL
secrets.purpose: Fan-out target for lib/ops/notify.mjs and several workflows (ralph-watchdog.yml, production-health.yml, parked-triggers.yml, notify-merge.yml) — every automated 'tell Adrian' alert goes through this one webhook.
secrets.breaksWhenMissing: Every one of those alerts fails soft (notifyEvent/postToDiscord never throw), so nothing crashes — but every page, merge notice and awaiting-approval ping goes silently nowhere. The same 'looks healthy, isn't' shape as ops#347, applied to the alert channel instead of the data path.
secrets.rotateUrl: Discord app → the target server → Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → regenerate the ops-alerts webhook (no fixed public URL — guild/channel IDs make every server's path different)

secrets.name: NPM_TOKEN
secrets.purpose: Publishes @hirobius/design-system to the public npm registry from release.yml's changesets publish step.
secrets.breaksWhenMissing: The release workflow's publish step 401s; a version bump can still merge (CI runs on RELEASE_PAT/GITHUB_TOKEN, not this) but never reaches npm — consumers stay on the old published version.
secrets.rotateUrl: https://www.npmjs.com/settings/hirobius/tokens — BEST-EFFORT GUESS from the @hirobius npm scope, not independently confirmed; verify the npm org/user login before relying on it

secrets.name: CHROMATIC_PROJECT_TOKEN
secrets.purpose: Publishes Storybook visual-regression baselines to Chromatic (chromatic.yml) — the visual verification surface since the Playwright test:layout suite retired (#161).
secrets.breaksWhenMissing: chromatic.yml fails to publish; PRs stop getting visual-diff review and Storybook baselines stop updating.

secrets.name: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN
secrets.purpose: Auth for hds's dispatched-task executor (claude.yml) — same pattern as the ops copy. hds's workflow comment says 'repo/org secret', so this may resolve from an org-level secret rather than a value stored in hds itself.
secrets.breaksWhenMissing: @claude-mentioned issues/comments in hds stop being picked up.
secrets.rotateUrl: run `claude setup-token` locally, then update the secret

secrets.name: DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL
secrets.breaksWhenMissing: hds merge notifications go silently nowhere; fails soft, so nothing in CI turns red.
secrets.rotateUrl: Discord app → the target server → Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → regenerate the webhook

secrets.name: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN
secrets.purpose: Auth for site-engine's dispatched-task executor (claude.yml) — same pattern as the ops copy.
secrets.breaksWhenMissing: @claude-mentioned issues/comments in site-engine stop being picked up.
secrets.rotateUrl: run `claude setup-token` locally, then update the secret

secrets.name: DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL
secrets.breaksWhenMissing: site-engine merge notifications go silently nowhere; fails soft, so nothing in CI turns red.
secrets.rotateUrl: Discord app → the target server → Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → regenerate the webhook

secrets.name: CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN
secrets.purpose: Declared in Ralph's REUSABLE workflows (ralph-run-reusable.yml, ralph-gate-reusable.yml, ralph-triage-reusable.yml) but resolved via `secrets: inherit` from the CALLING repo (ops/hds/site-engine) at invocation time. Ralph's own repo has no caller workflow that runs these against itself (only test.yml exists alongside the three reusable definitions, and it doesn't reference this secret) — verified by listing Ralph's .github/workflows/ directory.
secrets.breaksWhenMissing: Nothing in Ralph's own CI consumes this directly, so a missing copy IN RALPH breaks nothing there. The real failure is upstream: if ops/hds/site-engine's OWN copy of this secret lapses, `secrets: inherit` passes nothing through and the reusable workflow's Claude Code step fails in the CALLING repo, not here — those repos' own registry entries are what actually needs watching.
secrets.rotateUrl: run `claude setup-token` locally, then update the secret — only relevant if Ralph ever gains a caller workflow of its own

secrets.name: DISCORD_WEBHOOK_URL
secrets.purpose: Same inherit-only nature as the CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN entry above — declared in Ralph's reusable workflows, resolved from the calling repo via `secrets: inherit`, never consumed by a workflow that runs directly in Ralph's own repo.
secrets.breaksWhenMissing: Nothing in Ralph's own CI consumes this directly. The failure that matters is the calling repo's own copy lapsing — see the CLAUDE_CODE_OAUTH_TOKEN entry above.
secrets.rotateUrl: Discord app → the target server → Server Settings → Integrations → Webhooks → regenerate the webhook — only relevant if Ralph ever gains a caller workflow of its own
